definition.counted_on: train split, iscrowd excluded (D6) — the instances the model learned from

operating_threshold.source: max-F1 operating point for model '640' read from /Users/jen/Projects/coding/computervision/reports/metrics/thresholds.json

common.interpretation: 6 classes with >=500 train instances: 13718 train and 1607 val objects. Mean per-class AP50-95 0.1497 (middle of the three bands), recall 0.4362. Why it matters: D13 measured a severe imbalance (person alone is ~31% of annotations) and chose to expose it at evaluation rather than resample, so this is where that promise is kept. What it reveals: this band sets the recall ceiling, but data volume does not buy per-class accuracy — the head classes are also the small, cluttered ones (person, chair, bottle, cup, book), so frequency and difficulty are confounded.

mid.interpretation: 59 classes with 100-499 train instances, 1778 val objects. Mean per-class AP50-95 0.1470 (98% of the common band, lowest of the three), recall 0.2238 (51% of common). Why it matters: COCO mAP is a macro-average over classes, so these 59 of 80 classes effectively set the headline number even though they are a minority of the objects. What it reveals: the frequency effect shows up in recall at a fixed confidence, not in AP — the scores of mid-frequency classes rank fine but sit below the threshold.

rare.interpretation: 15 classes with <100 train instances and only 95 val objects between them (D4 flagged the extremes: toaster 11 and hair drier 6 train instances). Mean per-class AP50-95 0.1589 (106% of the common band, highest of the three), recall 0.2842 (65% of common). Why it matters: this is the tail the assignment's imbalance question is about. What it reveals: rarity costs recall at the operating point, not ranking quality — several rare classes are large, visually distinctive objects (microwave, bear, fire hydrant, stop sign) that score well, while the truly starved ones sit at zero. The band mean is statistically fragile: with a handful of val objects per class, one detection moves a class's AP substantially, so read it as indicative, and read per_class_{label}_val.md for the per-class detail.
